claims.explanation: Vorinostat is a pan-HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by dependence on class I HDAC activity and intact apoptotic/transcriptional programs rather than by a single lineage. Lines with TP53 pathway loss, PI3K/PTEN alterations, or other proliferative/survival dependencies tend to be more sensitive, while lines with EGFR activation, mesenchymal/mesothelioma identity, or high NF1/RAS-MAPK and chromatin-remodeler mutations are relatively protected. The virtual-cell response (MYC, CDC20, BIRC5 down; DNAJB1, HMOX1 up) supports a mechanism involving HDAC-dependent MYC/anti-apoptotic gene expression and stress-response induction.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set; loss of p53-mediated apoptosis may increase reliance on HDAC-regulated survival pathways
PIK3CA-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, suggesting PI3K-driven survival is HDAC-dependent
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, which can sensitize to HDAC inhibition
NF1 loss with RAS/MAPK activation appears in several sensitive lines
Virtual cell shows MYC downregulation; MYC-driven lines may depend on HDAC activity
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines are among the least affected, suggesting EGFR signaling bypasses HDAC dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines appear in both sets but several are resistant, suggesting MAPK-driven survival
NF2-mutant lines appear among sensitive lines, possibly via Hippo/YAP dependence on HDAC
ARID1A loss may create chromatin-state vulnerability to HDAC inhibition
KMT2D mutations appear in several sensitive lines, suggesting altered chromatin regulation
SMARCA4-mutant lines are among the least affected, suggesting SWI/SNF loss reduces HDAC dependence
Higher class I HDAC expression may increase dependence on HDAC activity
